Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier this week. Attached is our SIG worksheet (attached: SIG_Questions_HealthMerge_20270618.xlsx) — there are a few clarifications we need on the data handling / training / retention sections before we proceed to procurement:

1) Prompt & transient logs: Can you confirm the default retention window for request/response logs and whether that is configurable per-customer (we'd like to be able to set 7 days)? Also please describe where those logs are stored (S3 in customer VPC / Redwood-controlled storage / other) and whether they are accessible to Redwood ops for debugging.

2) Model training: Does Redwood use customer prompt/response data to continue-training or fine-tune any models? If so, is there an explicit opt-out and what is the mechanism? We need a signed attestation or a link to the policy.

3) KV/prefix cache / ephemeral state: For features like conversation memory / KV cache, how long does cached state persist, and is that persisted to durable storage at any point?

4) Deletion & evidence: If we request deletion of logs for a specific tenant, can you provide a timestamped deletion confirmation and the audit trail (who/what deleted, job id)? Example redacted output would be useful.

We appreciate short, direct answers and any supporting artifacts (attestations, runbooks, sample deletion logs).

Best,
Lisa Park
Head of Security Operations | HealthMerge

Attachment: SIG_Questions_HealthMerge_20270618.xlsx (Excel worksheet)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG: data handling questions for HealthMerge

Hi Lisa — thanks for the worksheet, and great questions. Below are concise answers and pointers; attaching our short attestation and an editable SIG response workbook (Training_Retention_Attestation.pdf & SIG_Responses_HealthMerge.xlsx). If you want a follow-up call, happy to arrange.

1) Prompt & transient logs:
- Default retention: 30 days for request/response request traces in hosted Redwood API.
- Configurable: Yes — retention is configurable per-customer for both Hosted and Dedicated plans. For Dedicated/Private we can set a 7-day retention window as a configuration flag; for Hosted we offer per-tenant retention profiles with a minimum of 7 days.
- Storage location: By default logs are stored in encrypted object storage managed by Redwood (AWS S3, separate buckets per tenant). For Private/VPC deployments logs can be stored in customer-managed buckets in their VPC (we will provide Terraform modules/guide).
- Ops access: Access to these logs is strictly role-based and audited. Debugging access requires an access request that is approved by the on-call owner; all accesses are recorded in our access audit logs.

2) Model training:
- Redwood does NOT use customer production prompt/response data to train or fine-tune our public models by default. We have a strict policy: training on customer data requires explicit, written opt-in.
- Opt-out: Customers are opted-out by default. If a customer chooses to participate in aggregate training programs, we require a signed addendum and a tokenized opt-in flag on the account.
- Attestation: Attached: Training_Retention_Attestation.pdf — short attestation signed by our security lead describing the default opt-out posture and the opt-in process.

3) KV/prefix cache and ephemeral state:
- Inference runtime caches (KV caches, prefix caches) are ephemeral in-memory structures tied to the instance and the request lifetime. They are not flushed to durable storage as part of normal operation.
- For autoscale or checkpointing scenarios where we persist state to speed up cold-starts, we use encrypted short-lived artifacts with a default TTL of 1 hour; these artifacts are stored in transient object storage and are periodically garbage-collected.

4) Deletion & evidence:
- We support on-demand tenant log deletion. Deletion jobs are recorded with job id, initiator (service or user id), timestamp, and checksum of removed objects. We can provide a redacted example deletion log (see runbook-delete-sample.txt attached).
- Time-to-complete: For Hosted accounts, deletion jobs typically complete within 24–72 hours depending on dataset size; Dedicated/Private deployments can have shorter SLA depending on storage location.

Next steps:
- I can provide a redacted deletion log example and a template MFA-approved deletion request workflow.
- Marissa (CS) — can you confirm whether HealthMerge is on Hosted or Dedicated plan for this procurement? That will affect the exact retention options.

References / links:
- Evidence folder: https://drive.redwood.company/HealthMerge/SIG/evidence-2027-06-21

Thanks,

Lisa — quick status update and promised artifacts. Forwarding redacted examples and runbook; see attachments and Drive link. Quoted below are the key confirmations so procurement can proceed.

> Hosted minimum retention enforcement
- Confirmed: For Hosted with VPC connectors we can enforce a tenant-level retention policy with a minimum of 7 days. We will lock the tenant policy so it cannot be extended beyond the configured window without a documented change request.

> Deletion evidence sample
- Attached: runbook-delete-sample.txt (redacted example deletion job). The redacted snippet includes: job id (job-7f9a2), timestamp, initiator role ("Platform Ops - approved runbook"), and redacted object key patterns (s3://redwood-logs/healthmerge/tenant-***/requests/***).

> Operational notes
- Deletion jobs are executed by the platform worker with a two-step commit: mark-for-delete then purge. Both steps are recorded in the audit trail with separate job ids.
- We will provide an export of the audit trail for the tenant on request; exports include CSV with job ids, timestamps, initiators (roles), and checksums.

Marissa / Rishi — can we confirm delivery of the attached runbook and the signed attestation to Lisa by EOD? I have attached the files to this thread and uploaded them to the shared drive link above.

Ben
